analysis.title: US manufacturing benefiting from a strong economy, tech investment, tariffs and energy security
key_insights: October ISM manufacturing index rose to 55.5 from 54.5 in September, above the market expectation that it would hold at 54.5.
The ISM production index rose to 59.0 from 56.7, a five-year high, and new orders (55.5) and the order backlog (54.6) are both well above the 50 break-even level.
ISM employment slipped to 52.4 from 52.7, which ING says means manufacturing should still add to Friday's payrolls figure.
ISM prices paid are at 75.2, in line with their six-month average.
Performance is split. High value-added manufacturing (tech, electronics, transport, power-related) has significantly outperformed, and ING expects that to continue.
Traditional, labour-intensive, commoditised manufacturing will keep shrinking. Tariffs do not offset the high cost of US production, and retaliatory tariffs hurt these producers abroad.
Higher military spending in other countries may strengthen order books for US defence companies.
Construction spending fell 1.9% MoM in September after a 2% rise in August (first reported as +0.9%).
Residential construction rose 3.6% MoM in August and fell 5.5% in September. ING sees a clear downtrend driven by poor affordability at higher mortgage rates.
Non-residential construction is skewed to data centres, up 8.6% MoM and 90.3% YoY. Non-residential spending outside data centres and electric power is flat.

sector_views.rationale: Significantly outperformed other manufacturing sectors, helped by tariffs, energy security and strong US growth. ING expects this to continue.
Under pressure from foreign competitors, and tariffs do not offset high US production costs. Retaliatory tariffs also hurt these producers abroad.
More countries are raising military spending, which may strengthen US defence order books.
Spending is trending down because of poor affordability at higher mortgage rates.
